title: Buenos Aires and Iguazú
summary: Two short Buenos Aires stays bracket six nights at Iguazú. The falls get the weekend; weekdays are work from 8 to 3 with the late afternoons and evenings for the town, the river and the market. The Brazilian side and the bird park stay in the pool for whichever afternoon frees up.

tripMap.note: Custom map maintained by hand; it does not update when the plan changes.

notes: Weekdays are work days, 08:00–15:00 local, from a café or the room.
Argentina keeps UTC−3 all year; no clock change during the trip.

stays.name: Puerto Iguazú
stays.summary: The falls are the point: spend all of Sunday in the Argentine park, starting at the Garganta del Diablo before the crowds. Weekday evenings belong to the town — the hummingbird garden, the Three Frontiers at sunset, the Feirinha for dinner.
priorities: Brazilian side panorama if an afternoon frees up

lodging.name: Hotel in the town center
lodging.notes: Walking distance to the bus terminal.

stays.transport: Park buses from the town terminal; remises (taxis) for the Brazilian side. Bring passport for Brazil.

workRhythm.note: Hotel Wi-Fi can be weak; have a café backup.

notes: Humid and hot by midday; sun hat and water for the park.

stays.name: Buenos Aires
stays.summary: A free weekend: Recoleta and the bookshop on Saturday, the San Telmo street fair on Sunday before the flight home.

commitments.title: Gran Aventura boat ride
commitments.notes: Meet at the Gran Aventura stand inside the park 15 minutes early.

activities.name: Garganta del Diablo walkway
activities.short: Catwalk to the lip of the biggest fall
detail: Take the first park train from Estación Central to Estación Garganta, then the 1.1 km catwalk over the upper river to the viewing platform at the edge of the Devil's Throat.
Go first, before the tour groups arrive; the spray is heavy, so bag the phone.
Since the boat moved to the morning, go after lunch instead; the afternoon light on the spray is better anyway.
activities.why: The single strongest sight of the trip, and it is best with the place nearly empty.

place.name: Garganta del Diablo
place.query: Garganta del Diablo, Parque Nacional Iguazú

practical.booking: Park ticket at the gate or online; the train is included.

booking.how: Buy the park ticket online the day before to skip the gate queue.

activities.name: Upper Circuit (Circuito Superior)
activities.short: Catwalks along the top of the falls
detail: About 1.7 km of level catwalks running along the top edge of a dozen falls, with views down the gorge.

activities.name: Lower Circuit (Circuito Inferior)
activities.short: Trails and stairs below the falls
detail: A loop of trails and stairs through the forest under the falls, with close views of Salto Bossetti and the San Martín falls.
activities.why: The most varied walk in the park; pairs naturally with the boat ride, which leaves from its lower end.

activities.name: Gran Aventura boat ride
activities.short: Jungle truck, then a boat into the falls
detail: A truck ride through the forest down to the river, then a speedboat up the gorge and under the edge of the falls. You will be soaked.

place.query: Iguazú Jungle Gran Aventura, Parque Nacional Iguazú

practical.booking: Booked — see the commitment for the time.
practical.tips: Dry bag for phone and passport.

activities.name: Sendero Macuco
activities.short: Quiet jungle trail to a hidden waterfall
detail: A 3.5 km (each way) forest trail away from the crowds, ending at the Arrechea waterfall. Good odds of seeing coatis, toucans and monkeys early in the day.
activities.why: The only real hike in the park, and the quietest part of it.

activities.name: Brazilian side: Trilha das Cataratas
activities.short: The panorama the Argentine side can't show
detail: Cross the border to Parque Nacional do Iguaçu and walk the 1.2 km trail facing the whole curtain of falls, ending on a platform beside the Devil's Throat.
Pair with the bird park, which is next to the Brazilian park entrance.
activities.why: Argentina is for being inside the falls; Brazil is for seeing all of them at once.

place.query: Parque Nacional do Iguaçu, Foz do Iguaçu

practical.transport: Remis from town, about 30 min plus the border crossing.
practical.cost: Entry paid in Brazilian reais or by card.

activities.name: Parque das Aves
activities.short: Walk-through aviaries of Atlantic Forest birds
detail: Large walk-through aviaries with toucans, macaws and hummingbirds, run as a conservation center for Atlantic Forest species.

place.query: Parque das Aves, Foz do Iguaçu

activities.name: Jardín de los Picaflores
activities.short: A backyard full of hummingbirds
detail: A family garden in town with feeders that draw dozens of hummingbirds of several species. Small, close-up and unhurried.
activities.why: An hour that fits after a work day, and nothing else on the trip looks like it.

place.query: Jardín de los Picaflores, Puerto Iguazú

activities.name: Hito Tres Fronteras
activities.short: Sunset where three countries meet
detail: The landmark at the meeting of the Iguazú and Paraná rivers, looking across to Brazil and Paraguay. Walk there along the riverfront from the center.

activities.name: Güira Oga wildlife rescue
activities.short: Guided walk through a rescue center
detail: A rescue and rehabilitation center for injured and trafficked animals of the Atlantic Forest, visited on a guided walk.

activities.name: La Aripuca
activities.short: A giant bird-trap built from salvaged trees
detail: A huge structure built in the shape of a Guaraní bird trap from trunks of trees that had been felled, with a small exhibit on the forest.

activities.name: La Feirinha
activities.short: Evening market: cheese, cured meats, empanadas
detail: The covered market in town where stalls sell Argentine cheeses, salami, olives and wine; several have tables and grills for a casual dinner.
activities.why: Local, casual and good — the right dinner after a work day.

activities.name: Riverfront run on the Costanera
activities.short: Out-and-back along the Paraná
detail: Run from the center down to the riverfront avenue and out to the Hito Tres Fronteras and back, about 5 km.

activities.name: Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur
activities.short: Wild reserve on the river, next to downtown
detail: Trails through reeds and lagoons between Puerto Madero and the Río de la Plata, busy with runners and birders. The river edge at the far side is the reward.
activities.why: A real run or walk from downtown, with nature right next to the skyline.

place.query: Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur, Buenos Aires

activities.name: Bosques de Palermo run
activities.short: Loop around the lakes and rose garden
detail: Run the loops around the Palermo lakes and the Rosedal; the main route for runners in the city.

activities.name: MALBA
activities.short: Latin American art museum in Palermo
detail: The museum of Latin American art: Frida Kahlo, Tarsila do Amaral, Berni, Xul Solar.

activities.name: Don Julio
activities.short: The Palermo parrilla
detail: A classic Palermo steakhouse with a long wait; book ahead or go early.

booking.how: Reservations open two weeks ahead on their website; walk-ins wait over an hour.

activities.name: Café Tortoni
activities.short: The 1858 café on Avenida de Mayo
detail: The old grand café: go for the room, not the coffee.

activities.name: Feria de San Telmo
activities.short: Sunday street fair along Calle Defensa
detail: Antiques, street musicians and tango in Plaza Dorrego, stretching blocks along Defensa. Walk it end to end and finish in the covered Mercado de San Telmo.
activities.why: The city at its liveliest, and it only happens on Sundays.

place.query: Plaza Dorrego, San Telmo, Buenos Aires

activities.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta
activities.short: A city of marble mausoleums
detail: Avenues of ornate family tombs, Evita's among them. Pick up a map at the entrance.

place.query: Cementerio de la Recoleta, Buenos Aires

activities.name: El Ateneo Grand Splendid
activities.short: A bookshop inside a 1919 theatre
detail: A bookshop in a converted theatre, with the stage turned into a café.

place.query: El Ateneo Grand Splendid, Buenos Aires

activities.name: Itaipu Dam panoramic tour
activities.short: Bus tour of one of the world's largest dams
detail: A guided bus tour across the dam on the Brazil–Paraguay border, from the Brazilian visitor center north of Foz do Iguaçu.

place.query: Itaipu Binacional visitor center, Foz do Iguaçu

practical.access: Passport for the border; tours sell out on weekends.

days.title: Argentine falls
days.note: Boat at 10:30 first, then the Garganta del Diablo and the Upper Circuit; Lower Circuit to finish.

days.title: Work, then the market
days.note: Work; at 3 pm the hummingbird garden, then dinner at the Feirinha.

days.title: Recoleta
days.note: Recoleta cemetery in the morning, El Ateneo after lunch.

days.title: San Telmo and home
days.note: The San Telmo fair end to end, then pack for the 21:00 flight.
